text: A rotary encoder that provides a unique digital binary code for every discrete angular position, retaining exact shaft position through power cycles.
A high-pitched noise produced when motor windings vibrate from PWM switching frequencies that fall within the audible range of human hearing (20 Hz to 20 kHz).
A ROS communication pattern for long-running tasks that sends periodic progress feedback, can be canceled while running, and returns a final result when complete.
Unfair errors or discrimination in machine learning software, often caused by incomplete or unbalanced training data, such as a vision system failing to detect certain pedestrian groups.
A popular open-source microcontroller board used to prototype robot electronics, available as the classic 8-bit Uno R3 or the faster 32-bit Uno R4.
The two-argument arctangent atan2(y, x), which returns the angle of the point (x, y) in the correct quadrant, including when x = 0.
A collision object that has been fixed to a robot link in the planning scene, so it moves with the tool and is checked for collisions as part of the robot.
A machine that moves on its own using a built-in mechanism, such as clockwork gears, without sensing or adapting to the world around it (plural: automata).
The small play in a gear train that lets the output move slightly without the input moving, which robot reducers keep to about an arc-minute or less.
A lighting method placing the light source behind an object, producing a sharp black silhouette against a bright background for measuring part outlines and dimensions.
An optional part of a UR PolyScope program that runs once before the main program loop, used to put the robot and tools in a known state.
A tree of tasks that a robot program runs step by step; each node reports success, failure or running when it is ticked. Nav2 uses one to organize planning, control and recovery.
A ROS 2 Quality of Service policy that delivers messages quickly without waiting for acknowledgments or retransmitting lost packets, ideal for high-frequency sensor streams.
An open, two-way digital communication protocol for absolute encoders that lets a controller read exact shaft positions and exchange configuration or diagnostic data with the encoder.
A RAPID instruction that registers a user-defined error number with the controller so the program can raise and handle it like a system error.
The automated build and testing infrastructure at ci.ros2.org running nightly jobs across platforms and architectures.
A multi-stage edge detection algorithm that uses Gaussian smoothing, intensity gradients, non-maximum suppression, and hysteresis thresholding to find thin, robust boundaries.
A multi-loop control architecture where an outer position loop generates setpoints for an inner velocity loop, which in turn commands a high-speed current loop.
A solid-state image sensor where each pixel has its own amplifier and readout circuitry, enabling fast frame rates and low power consumption.
A lighting geometry using a beamsplitter to project diffuse light along the camera's optical axis, reducing shadows and glare on flat specular surfaces.
A document in a repository that sets ground rules for participant behavior, helping keep discussions constructive, respectful, and welcoming for all community members.
The electrical engineering practice of tying the 0V reference wires of multiple power supplies together so digital control signals share a common reference plane.
A simple fusion filter that trusts one sensor over short time spans and another over long ones, such as a gyroscope and accelerometer for tilt.
An MTC wrapper stage that turns the poses produced by the stage inside it, such as grasp poses, into joint configurations by solving inverse kinematics.
A situation where an engineer's personal, financial, or business interests could bias their professional judgment, or appear to. Ethical codes require engineers to disclose such conflicts promptly.
A digital multimeter test performed on de-energized, isolated circuits that triggers an audible beep when component resistance drops below a threshold.
The computer that runs the robot's program and decides what to do next, from a small microcontroller like an Arduino to an industrial robot controller.
The central component in ros2_control that manages controller lifecycles and connects them to hardware-abstraction interfaces to run the main control loop.
A programming approach where tasks share processor time by running brief non-blocking checks against a clock (such as millis()) instead of using blocking delays that freeze the CPU.
In Nav2, a regular 2D grid of cells, each marked as unknown, free, occupied or inflated, that planners search for a path and controllers sample to steer.
A technique using a polarizer on the light source and an analyzer on the camera lens oriented at 90 degrees to eliminate direct specular glare from reflective surfaces.
A ROS package providing bidirectional conversion functions between ROS Image messages and OpenCV NumPy array buffers.
A shallow-angle lighting technique where direct rays reflect away from the lens and surface flaws or scratches scatter light into the camera as bright features.
The privacy engineering principle mandating that systems collect, process, and retain only the minimal data strictly necessary for a specified function.
The list in an ament_python package's setup.py that tells the build which extra files, such as launch and YAML files, to copy into the install space.
One independent way a robot can move, with each revolute or prismatic joint adding one; a rigid object in space has six (three for position, three for orientation).
A parallel robot whose arms all connect to one tool plate so their links form a closed loop, built for fast, light pick-and-place.
A physical and logical subnet acting as an intermediary between corporate and control networks so connected devices avoid direct exposure to untrusted networks.
An industrial Ethernet ring topology featuring an active ring supervisor transmitting beacon frames, achieving a worst-case recovery time of 2890 µs on copper with default beacon settings.
An Arduino pin that is either HIGH (5 V) or LOW (0 V), used for simple on/off signals such as an LED or a bump switch.
The horizontal pixel difference between corresponding points in left and right stereo images. It is inversely proportional to depth, so closer objects produce larger disparity values.
A pull request opened before the work is finished, marked as a draft or work in progress, to get early feedback from reviewers.
The two mirror-image postures a two-link arm can use to reach the same point, with the elbow on one side or the other of the line from base to target.
The tool mounted on the robot's wrist flange that does the actual work, such as a gripper, vacuum cup, spot-welding gun or arc-welding torch.
The device mounted on a robot's flange that does the work, such as a gripper, suction cups or a welding torch; also called EOAT or the end effector.
A mechanical device capable of being locked out with a hasp, attachment point, or locking mechanism, excluding push buttons and control circuit devices.
The predefined RAPID variable that holds the number of the error being handled, so an error handler can react differently to different errors.
The ERROR section at the end of a RAPID routine, where execution jumps when an instruction in that routine fails, so the program can retry, skip, return or pass the error on.
A mechanism that lets a power source move a machine forward in small, regular steps; Su Song's clock tower, completed by 1094, used one.
A rule registered with the launch system that runs actions when something happens to a process, for example shutting everything down when a node exits.
A non-linear adaptation of the Kalman filter that linearizes dynamic and measurement functions locally around the current state estimate using first-order Taylor series Jacobian matrices.
A Universal Robots add-on that, when its node runs in a pendant program, fetches a URScript program from the ROS driver on the PC and runs it so ROS can command the arm.
A paid ABB RobotWare option that lets an external computer stream joint or pose targets to the robot controller over UDP at a fixed rate.
A camera setup in which the camera is mounted on the robot's gripper and moves with it.
A camera setup in which the camera is fixed in the cell and watches the work area while the robot moves.
An industrial digital network that replaces discrete point-to-point wiring by connecting sensors, actuators, and controllers over a single shared communication cable.
A system design pattern where a robot stays in exactly one state at a time, switching between defined states when specific sensor events or conditions occur.
The reference coordinate frame selected in RViz (such as 'map' or 'odom') against which all other incoming spatial transforms and sensor points are rendered.
A large AI model trained on massive amounts of data that can adapt to many tasks. In robotics, vision-language-action models turn camera images and user instructions directly into robot actions.
The separation of electrical circuits so no direct current flows between them, using components like intermediate relays to block ground loops and noise.
A 3D robot simulator with physics that simulates a robot, its sensors and its surroundings, and connects to ROS 2 so code can be tested before running on real hardware.
Parts of this site's files that scripts/site_sync.py builds automatically, such as the sitemap, hub rows and navigation bars; they are not edited by hand.
An MTC stage that creates robot states on its own, such as the current state or a set of candidate grasp poses, without needing a neighboring stage's result.
A formula, DOF = m(N − 1 − J) + Σfᵢ, that counts a mechanism's degrees of freedom from its number of links, joints and joint freedoms.
An electronic circuit topology consisting of four switching elements arranged in an 'H' configuration, enabling bidirectional current flow through DC motor coils.
AI output that looks confident and plausible but is not grounded in fact, such as a function or package that does not exist.
Finding the fixed transform between a camera and the robot gripper (or robot base), usually by solving the AX = XB equation from several robot poses.
A pair of request and reply signals that a PLC and a robot exchange so that each one waits for the other before going on.
A ros2_control plugin that reads joint states from and writes commands to a specific robot, real or simulated, so the controllers above it do not need to know the brand.
A processor mechanism that halts normal program execution immediately upon an electrical pin state change to execute an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR).
An error in a mobile robot's estimated orientation; because every later step is driven in the wrong direction, a small heading error grows into a large sideways (lateral) position error.
A calibration routine where a robot moves its joints to physical limit switches or index marks to establish a known zero-reference coordinate frame.
A design in which a person can understand, check and override what an automated system does.
A robot with a roughly human body shape, usually with two legs and two arms, built to work in spaces designed for people.
A table of every input and output signal in a cell, with its name, number and meaning, such as which output closes the gripper.
The annual statistical report published by the International Federation of Robotics tracking factory robot installations, operational stock, and robot density across countries worldwide.
Weighted calculations of pixel intensities across an image contour used to determine geometric properties such as part area, orientation, and center-of-mass (centroid) coordinates.
A ROS 2 package suite providing transparent runtime plugin support for publishing and subscribing to compressed image streams.
A URScript command that converts an integer into a little-endian list of boolean values where the first element is the least significant bit.
A condition where an integrator accumulates excessive error while the actuator is saturated, causing severe overshoot and delay upon desaturation.
A signal that makes a microcontroller pause its main program and run a short handler straight away, for example when an encoder pin changes.
The matrix that converts joint speeds into tool velocity; when its determinant is zero, the robot is at a singularity.
Joseph-Marie Jacquard's 1804 loom attachment that used chains of punched cards to control the woven pattern, an early example of a machine run by a stored program.
An optimal recursive data processing algorithm that estimates the internal state of a linear dynamic system from a series of noisy measurements over time.
A dynamic weighting factor between 0 and 1 that balances trust between a projected system model and incoming noisy sensor measurements to minimize estimation error covariance.
A high-level compiled programming language used on FANUC robot controllers for data handling, file access, and network socket communication alongside everyday teach-pendant motion programs.
The integral gain of a PID controller, which sets how strongly accumulated past error adds to the output to remove a lingering offset.
An AI model trained on very large amounts of text that predicts likely next words, which lets it answer questions and write code.
The object a ROS 2 launch file returns: a list of actions, such as nodes to start, that the launch system carries out.
A programming method in which the programmer physically guides the robot arm through the waypoints of a task while the robot records them; it is the main method for cobots.
A sensor that measures distances with laser light; a spinning 2D LiDAR sweeps a beam around the robot to map its surroundings in one plane.
A move in which the controller drives the TCP along a straight line in Cartesian space, as opposed to a joint move (MoveJ) in which all joints move together and the tool path is curved.
Lithium polymer rechargeable battery common in mobile robots for its high energy density; Battery University gives about 3.6 V nominal per cell, and hobby packs are often labeled slightly higher.
Automated USB backup scripts on Universal Robots controllers that automatically copy programs, installation files, and system configuration as soon as the drive is inserted.
A world-fixed frame in which the robot's pose does not drift but can jump when localization corrects it.
A wheeled robot, such as Sojourner, Curiosity or Perseverance, that explores the surface of Mars while scientists on Earth plan its routes and experiments.
A modern, high-performance container file format designed specifically for robotics telemetry and multimodal sensor logging in ros2 bag.
A software layer sitting between the operating system and user programs that handles communication, message passing, and hardware coordination across different robot devices.
An Arduino function that returns the milliseconds since the board started, used to time events without blocking; it wraps to zero after about 50 days.
A robot that moves through its environment instead of staying bolted in place, such as a warehouse robot or planetary rover, and relies on sensors to map, localize and plan paths.
A ros2_control stand-in for a real robot that simply copies each command into its state, so software can be tested with no robot or physics.
